title: 90832 CPT Code: Time Range and Documentation Requirements
summary: The 90832 CPT code is psychotherapy for 16 to 37 minutes. Time rules, 90833 with E/M, 2026 Medicare rates, telehealth and what the note must show.
body_markdown:
**The 90832 CPT code is individual psychotherapy with the patient for 16 to 37 minutes.** It is the shortest of the three timed psychotherapy codes. In 2026 Medicare pays USD 85.84 nationally in the office, before your locality adjustment.


Most 90832 problems come from two errors. Contacts under 16 minutes get billed anyway. Prescribers bill 90832 next to an E/M code when the add-on 90833 was required. This guide covers the time rule, the 2026 rates, the add-on codes, telehealth and what the note must show.


**Key takeaways**


- 90832 is individual psychotherapy for 16 to 37 minutes. Under 16 minutes, no psychotherapy code applies.
- With an E/M visit such as 99214, bill the add-on 90833, never 90832.
- 2026 Medicare pays USD 85.84 nationally in the office and USD 69.47 in a facility, before locality.
- Medicare allows up to 2 units of 90832 per patient per day, each backed by its own documented time.


## What is CPT code 90832?


The CPT descriptor is "Psychotherapy, 30 minutes with patient." The CMS 2026 relative value file lists it as "Psytx w pt 30 minutes." The 30 minutes names a typical session. The billable range is 16 to 37 minutes.


Element 90832


Descriptor Psychotherapy, 30 minutes with patient


Billable time 16 to 37 minutes


Code type Standalone psychotherapy code


With an E/M visit Use the add-on[90833](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/90833-cpt-code) instead


Next code up[90834](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/90834-cpt-code) , from 38 minutes


2026 Medicare, non facility USD 85.84 national (2.57 RVU)


2026 Medicare, facility USD 69.47 national (2.08 RVU)


Telehealth Allowed, with place of service 02 or 10


Common add-on 90785 interactive complexity


## How many minutes is 90832?


16 to 37 minutes. The timed psychotherapy codes follow the midpoint rule. A session qualifies for a code once it passes the midpoint between that code and the one below. The same tiers apply to the add-on codes used with E/M.


Psychotherapy time Standalone code Add-on with E/M


Under 16 minutes No psychotherapy code No add-on


16 to 37 minutes 90832[90833](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/90833-cpt-code)


38 to 52 minutes[90834](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/90834-cpt-code) 90836


53 minutes or more[90837](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/90837-cpt-code) 90838


What counts toward the time:


- Face-to-face psychotherapy with the patient, or with the patient and a family member when the patient is present for all or part of it
- Time on a live video connection, for a telehealth session
- Psychotherapy time only. Time spent on the E/M part of a visit does not count.
- Not counted: charting after the session, scheduling, phone tag or a dropped connection
- Record start and stop times, or the total minutes, in the note
- Medicare allows up to 2 units per patient per day (practitioner MUE, October 2026). A second session needs its own documented time. Some payers allow only one.


## What do you bill for a session under 16 minutes?


No psychotherapy code. A 12 minute contact does not support 90832, however useful it was. What happens next depends on who delivered it.


- A prescriber: a short contact about medication is usually an E/M service, chosen by medical decision making
- A therapist: a contact under 16 minutes is generally not separately billable


Billing 90832 for contacts under 16 minutes looks deliberate in an audit, even when each claim was made in good faith.


## 90832 vs 90834 vs 90837


The three standalone codes differ only by time. The 2026 Medicare national amounts below use the January release of the CMS relative value file.


Code Time Total RVU, non facility National amount, non facility National amount, facility


90832 16 to 37 min 2.57 USD 85.84 USD 69.47


[90834](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/90834-cpt-code) 38 to 52 min 3.41 USD 113.90 USD 91.85


[90837](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/90837-cpt-code) 53 min or more 5.00 USD 167.00 USD 135.27


- A 38 minute session billed as 90832 leaves USD 28.06 per session unclaimed at the Medicare national rate
- Ten of those a month is USD 280.60 a month for one clinician
- Source: CMS PPRRVU2026_Jan_nonQPP, conversion factor 33.4009


## What is the difference between 90832 and 90833?


90832 stands alone. 90833 is an add-on for the same 16 to 37 minutes of psychotherapy, given in the same visit as an E/M service by a prescriber.


90832 90833


Code type Standalone Add-on, billed only with an E/M code


Who bills it Any eligible psychotherapy provider Prescribers who also bill the E/M visit


Time 16 to 37 minutes 16 to 37 minutes of psychotherapy, separate from E/M time


2026 Medicare, non facility USD 85.84 USD 81.50, on top of the E/M code


2026 Medicare, facility USD 69.47 USD 65.80, on top of the E/M code


Billed with 99214 No Yes


## Can you bill 99214 and 90832 together?


No. When psychotherapy happens in the same visit as an E/M service, it is reported with an add-on code. A prescriber who bills 99214 adds 90833, never 90832.


- 90833 for 16 to 37 minutes of psychotherapy with E/M (USD 81.50 non facility in 2026)
- 90836 for 38 to 52 minutes (USD 103.21)
- 90838 for 53 minutes or more (USD 136.61)
- The add-ons are tiered by time only. They are billed by video under the same rules as the base codes.
- Document the psychotherapy minutes separately. Time counted for psychotherapy cannot also support the E/M level.


Practices with prescribers and therapists usually get this wrong on the prescribers' claims. Our[guide to psychiatric billing](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/the-complete-guide-to-psychiatric-billing-from-e-m-to-psychotherapy-with-ai-powered-support) shows how the two code families fit together.


## How much does 90832 pay in 2026?


The CMS 2026 relative value file, January release, sets 90832 at 2.57 total RVUs non facility and 2.08 facility. At the 2026 conversion factor of 33.4009 that is USD 85.84 and USD 69.47 nationally.


Billed as Total RVU, non facility National amount, non facility Total RVU, facility National amount, facility


90832 2.57 USD 85.84 2.08 USD 69.47


90832 + 90785 3.01 USD 100.54 2.43 USD 81.16


90833 (add-on to E/M) 2.44 USD 81.50 1.97 USD 65.80


90834 3.41 USD 113.90 2.75 USD 91.85


90837 5.00 USD 167.00 4.05 USD 135.27


What changes the amount you are paid:


- Locality: your Medicare contractor adjusts the national amount by region. Look yours up in the[CMS Physician Fee Schedule Look-Up Tool](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/physician-fee-schedule/search) .
- Provider type: Medicare pays clinical social workers, marriage and family therapists and mental health counselors 75% of the amount
- Nurse practitioners, clinical nurse specialists and physician assistants are paid 85%
- Place of service: facility settings, and Medicare telehealth billed with place of service 02, pay the facility amount
- Commercial and Medicaid plans set their own rates by contract


## Who can bill 90832?


For Medicare, the[CMS Billing and Coding: Psychiatry and Psychology Services](https://www.cms.gov/medicare-coverage-database/view/article.aspx?articleId=57480) article sets the baseline. These practitioners can bill psychotherapy within their state scope of practice:


- Physicians (MDs and DOs)
- Clinical psychologists
- Clinical social workers
- Nurse practitioners
- Clinical nurse specialists
- Physician assistants
- Marriage and family therapists
- Mental health counselors


Where commercial and Medicaid plans differ:


- Some require start and stop times in the note
- Some do not credential every license type, such as associate-level clinicians
- Where a supervisor must bill, the claim needs the supervisor's NPI as rendering provider
- Some state Medicaid programs require a license-level modifier, such as HO, HN, AH or AJ, and pay by license level. Check your state fee schedule.
- In an FQHC, RHC or CCBHC paid a PPS rate, report 90832 on the claim. The clinic is paid its encounter or daily rate.


## Can 90832 be billed for telehealth?


Yes. The code does not change. The claim shows where the patient was.


Where the patient is Place of service Medicare pays


At home 10, telehealth in the patient's home Non facility amount


Somewhere other than home 02, telehealth outside the home Facility amount


In the office 11 Non facility amount


- Add modifier 95 where the payer asks for it
- Record in the note that the session was by video or audio, and where the patient was
- Audio-only to the patient's home: modifier 93 for Medicare
- Leave time lost to a dropped connection out of the billed minutes
- Our[place of service codes guide](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/place-of-service-codes) covers 02, 10 and 11 in detail


## Which add-on codes and modifiers go with 90832?


Code or modifier Use with 90832? Notes


90785 interactive complexity Yes, when a qualifying factor is documented Maladaptive communication among participants, a caregiver whose behavior gets in the way of the treatment plan, a sentinel event reported to a third party, or play equipment or an interpreter needed because the patient lacks expressive language. Never for interpretation alone, a hard session or extra time.


90833, 90836, 90838 No These replace 90832 when an E/M service is billed


99354, 99355 No Deleted from CPT. No prolonged service code applies to psychotherapy.


99417 (G2212 for Medicare) No Only with the highest-level office E/M visits, never with psychotherapy codes


Modifier 95 Sometimes Telehealth, where the payer requires it


90791 same day Usually no Payers generally reject psychotherapy on the same day as a[90791](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/90791-cpt-code) evaluation by the same provider


A session that runs past 37 minutes becomes 90834. Crisis and family sessions have their own codes.[90839](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/90839-cpt-code) covers crisis psychotherapy of 30 to 74 minutes, and[90846](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/90846-cpt-code) covers family psychotherapy without the patient present.


## What must a 90832 note document?


- Start and stop times, or total minutes, showing at least 16
- The psychotherapy approach used, such as CBT or supportive therapy
- The presenting problem and current status
- What was done in this session, specific enough to tell it apart from the last one
- The patient's response
- The plan and the reason for the next contact
- In person or telehealth, and the patient's location for telehealth
- Signature and credentials that match the rendering provider on the claim


If a short session is the clinical plan, say so in the note. A documented reason for a brief session holds up better than a note that reads like a cut-short hour. See our[SOAP note example](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/soap-note-example) for a structure these fields fit into.


## What does a 90832 note look like?


An example for a fictional patient, in the order a reviewer reads it:


- **Time:** 2:04 pm to 2:31 pm, 27 minutes, in person (place of service 11)
- **Presenting problem:** panic symptoms before work meetings, two episodes this week
- **Intervention:** CBT. Reviewed the panic log, practiced paced breathing, identified one thought to test
- **Response:** engaged, rated anxiety 7/10 at start and 4/10 at end
- **Plan:** continue the log, test the thought at Thursday's meeting, next session in one week
- **Signed:** licensed clinician, credentials matching the claim


A note reading "discussed anxiety, session went well" supports no code under review. It records that contact happened and nothing about the psychotherapy.

## Why do 90832 claims get denied?


Denial cause How it happens Fix


Under 16 minutes A short check-in billed as 90832 Do not bill a psychotherapy code under 16 minutes


Billed with an E/M code 99213 or 99214 plus 90832 on one claim Use the add-on 90833


No time in the note The note has no minutes Record start and stop times or total time


Same day as 90791 Evaluation and psychotherapy by the same provider Bill the evaluation for that date


Wrong rendering provider Associate billed under their own NPI Bill under the supervisor where the plan requires it


Telehealth details missing No place of service 02 or 10, or a missing modifier Match the payer's telehealth rules


Prolonged code attached 99354 or 99417 added for a long session Bill 90834 or 90837 by time


Vague note No intervention or response recorded Document what was done and how the patient responded


## What should you check before a 90832 claim goes out?


1. The note shows 16 to 37 minutes of psychotherapy, with times
2. No E/M code on the same claim, or the add-on 90833 is used instead
3. No 90791 by the same provider on the same date
4. Place of service matches where the patient was: 11, 02 or 10
5. Telehealth modifier 95 or audio-only modifier 93 where the payer requires it
6. 90785 only with a documented qualifying factor
7. Rendering NPI matches the clinician who signed, or the supervisor where required
8. Any Medicaid license-level modifier your state requires


## Why does session time get misremembered?


Most 90832 coding errors happen while the note is being reconstructed. A clinician charting after the last session recalls six or eight sessions, and memory drifts toward the schedule. A 40 minute session in a 30 minute slot gets remembered as 30 minutes and billed as 90832.


- The error runs one way, toward the calendar, so it shows up as undercoding
- Undercoded claims pay cleanly, so no denial report catches them
- Overcoding is the opposite risk: an audit that finds a pattern can reach back across past claims
- The fix is the same for both: capture the minutes while the session runs


## How do you check a practice for undercoded 90832 claims?


1. Pull a sample of 90832 claims from the last 90 days
2. Compare the minutes in each note with the code billed
3. Count the notes that document 38 minutes or more
4. Multiply that count by your contracted difference between 90834 and 90832
5. Refile only where the original note already supports the longer code, within each payer's correction window
6. Fix how time is captured, so the gap does not come back

## 90832 CPT code FAQ


### What is CPT code 90832?


Individual psychotherapy with the patient, 30 minutes. It is billed for 16 to 37 minutes of face-to-face psychotherapy.


### How many minutes is 90832?


16 to 37 minutes. Under 16 minutes, no psychotherapy code applies. From 38 minutes, bill 90834.


### What is the difference between 90832 and 90833?


90832 is a standalone psychotherapy code. 90833 is the add-on for 16 to 37 minutes of psychotherapy in the same visit as an E/M service. It is never billed alone.


### Can you bill 99214 and 90832 together?


No. With an E/M code such as 99214, the psychotherapy goes on the claim as the add-on 90833.


### How much does 90832 pay in 2026?


The 2026 Medicare national amount is USD 85.84 non facility and USD 69.47 facility, before the locality adjustment. Commercial rates are set by contract.


### Can 90832 be billed for telehealth?


Yes. The code stays the same. The claim carries the telehealth place of service, 02 or 10, and modifier 95 where the payer asks for it.


### Can 90785 be added to 90832?


Yes, when the note documents a qualifying factor, such as maladaptive communication among participants or a caregiver who interferes with the treatment plan. An interpreter alone does not qualify. It adds USD 14.70 non facility in 2026.


### Who can bill 90832?


For Medicare: physicians, clinical psychologists, clinical social workers, nurse practitioners, clinical nurse specialists, physician assistants, marriage and family therapists and mental health counselors.


### How many units of 90832 can you bill per day?


Medicare allows up to 2 units per patient per day under its October 2026 practitioner MUE table. Each session needs its own documented time. Some commercial and Medicaid plans allow only one.


### If a session ran 38 minutes but the note says 35, which code do you bill?


90832. The note is the evidence. A late entry can correct a factual error if it is dated and signed when written. It should never add minutes nobody recorded.
